diagnostic_evidence.quote: This transformation preserves the sufficient regularity of the integrand and hence improves the rate of convergence of RQMC.

Unbounded integrands do not satisfy the assumptions of the Koksma--Hlawka error bound (i.e., the variation of the integrand in the sense of Hardy and Krause is infinite); thus, the rate of convergence of RQMC may deteriorate.
Consequently, the entire transformed integrand is bounded near the boundary.

Consequently, the estimator \eqref{qmc_estimator} may achieve a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1 + \epsilon_r})$ \cite{owen2006halton}, with $\epsilon_r> 0$, depending on the regularity of $g(\cdot)$ and the dimension, $d$, of the domain.

issues.failure_explanation: What is claimed: the derived boundary growth conditions (i) preserve sufficient integrand regularity and (ii) ensure the nearly optimal RQMC rate O(N^{-1+eps}). What is established: only lim_{u_j->0}|r_j(u_j)|<infty, i.e. boundedness of g/psi o Psi^{-1} at the 2^d corners of [0,1]^d (e.g. 'lim_{u_j -> 0 }  \mid \tilde{g}(\boldsymbol{u}) \mid < \infty'). Boundedness does not imply the finite Hardy--Krause variation that the paper's own Koksma--Hlawka criterion requires, nor the mixed-derivative growth bounds and corner-avoidance hypotheses of the cited Owen-type theorem; neither is verified anywhere. Indeed at the critical parameter values the paper adopts (e.g. tilde{sigma}_j = 1/(sqrt(T) sigma_j), tilde{nu}=2T/nu-1, Sigma tilde = Sigma^{-1}) one has g tilde (u) ~ const * g-hat(Psi^{-1}(u)) with Psi^{-1}(u) ~ |log u|^{1/2}, while d Psi^{-1}/du = 1/psi(Psi^{-1}(u)) blows up exponentially; hence |partial g tilde / partial u_j| is not integrable and V_HK(g tilde)=infty, so the paper's own stated error bound is vacuous. The gap between boundedness and a proved near-optimal rate is therefore a missing nontrivial argument.

failure_location.quote: we tune the parameters of the proposal density to satisfy the derived boundary growth conditions that ensure nearly optimal convergence rates.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either supply the missing nontrivial lemma verifying the growth conditions on g tilde and all its mixed partials together with the corner-avoidance property of the employed randomized Sobol points (possibly requiring a stricter-than-critical choice of the transformation parameters), or downgrade the claim to what is proved (the transformation makes the transformed integrand bounded at the boundary, and the experiments exhibit near-optimal rates).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised theoretical guarantee (nearly optimal RQMC convergence rate O(N^{-1+eps}) under the derived parameter conditions) is unsupported for all three models and all dimensions; only boundedness of the transformed integrand and the empirical convergence plots remain. The claim in the abstract that the transformation 'preserves the sufficient regularity of the integrand' is likewise unestablished.
issues.title: Boundary growth conditions prove only boundedness but are advertised as ensuring near-optimal RQMC rates
issues.why_classification: The transformation construction, the boundedness statements, the parameter rules and every numerical result survive intact; what is lost is the proved rate guarantee. A contained nontrivial regularity lemma (or a limited downgrade of the guarantee while retaining the method and its demonstrated performance) is enough, so this is more than a local edit but needs no new global proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated convention P-hat(z)=int e^{+i z'x}P(x)dx, the integrand of the displayed formula pairs X_T with -x: int dy exp(i y'(xi+x)) = (2 pi)^d delta(xi+x) gives (2 pi)^{-d} e^{-rT} Re int Phi(y+iR) P-hat(y+iR) dy = e^{-rT} E[P(-X_T)], not e^{-rT} E[P(X_T)]. E.g. for the d=1 basket put P(x)=(1-e^x)^+ this returns the price of (1-e^{-X_T})^+, a different option. The formula is correct only with P-hat(z)=int e^{-i z'x}P(x)dx, which is exactly the convention matched by the table entries (for the basket put int_0^1 t^{-iz-1}(1-t)dt = Gamma(-iz)/Gamma(-iz+2), convergent iff Im z_j>0). Correspondingly delta_P must be built from e^{+<R,x>}P(x) in L^1: for P(x)=max(1-sum e^{x_i},0) -> 1 as x->-infinity, e^{-<R,x>}P(x) is not integrable for R>0, so under the stated definition delta_P is the opposite half-space from the table's {Im[z_j]>0} used in every experiment (R_j=4.44, 1.31, 5.73 > 0).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign in the definition of P-hat (e^{i z'x} -> e^{-i z'x}), correspondingly replace e^{-<R,x>} by e^{+<R,x>} in the definition of delta_P and in the L-infinity bound used in the GBM analysis, so that the valuation formula, the payoff table and the assumed strip agree.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition (QOI) is false as written; the strip delta_P in the payoff table and all damping vectors R used numerically lie outside the delta_P defined in the assumptions, so the hypothesis 'R in delta_V = delta_X cap delta_P' of the proposition is not met by the computations. All downstream pricing formulas are only valid after the convention is reconciled.
issues.title: Definition of P-hat and of delta_P has the opposite sign convention from the valuation formula and the payoff table
issues.why_classification: The corrections are sign repairs confined to the notation, the payoff assumption and one supporting inequality; the valuation formula, the payoff transforms, the strips, all parameter rules, rates and experiments are preserved unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The derived condition for a bounded ratio r_j^{VG} is tilde{nu} <= 2T/nu - 1 with tilde{nu}>0. The advised rule tilde{nu}=max(2T/nu-1,1) returns 1 whenever 2T/nu-1<1, i.e. it selects tilde{nu} > 2T/nu-1, which is precisely case (i) of eq:vg_conditions where h_1^{VG} -> +infinity at u_j -> 0. The rule is therefore wrong on the whole range 0 < 2T/nu-1 < 1 (where the valid choice tilde{nu}=2T/nu-1 is discarded), and for 2T/nu-1 <= 0 no admissible tilde{nu}>0 exists at all, so the derived conditions are vacuous on that regime; eq:vg_sigma_choice is also undefined there since it involves a negative power of tilde{nu}=2T/nu-1 <= 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use tilde{nu} = 2T/nu-1 (or 2T/nu-1 minus a small epsilon) whenever 2T/nu-1 > 0, and for 2T/nu <= 1 either explicitly restrict the VG scope or add the payoff-transform decay estimate that the paper only asserts informally to show that g-hat times r^{VG} stays bounded.
issues.overall_effect: For VG with 2T/nu < 2 the prescribed transformation parameter violates the paper's own boundary growth condition, so the transformed integrand ratio blows up at the boundary of [0,1] and the claimed regularity/rate guarantee is void; for 2T/nu <= 1 (short maturity or large nu) the derived conditions admit no solution at all, excluding a regime the paper advertises to cover.
issues.title: Recommended VG floor rule for tilde{nu} violates the derived boundary growth condition
issues.why_classification: The correction to the rule is local for 2T/nu>1, but a complete resolution of the 2T/nu<=1 regime needs the nontrivial payoff-decay bound the paper only suggests, or a restriction of the advertised regime; it does not require new global proof architecture, so it is more than minor but less than serious.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's own asymptotic eq:lap_pdf_as_exp retains the factors (q/2)^{v/2} and 1/sqrt(2 sqrt(2q)) with q = (Psi^{-1})' Sigma tilde^{-1} Psi^{-1}, i.e. psi_lap ~ C s^{(1-d)/2} e^{-s} with s = sqrt(2q). Hence 1/psi_lap ~ C^{-1} s^{(d-1)/2} e^{s}, so r^{NIG} = phi/psi_lap carries an additional factor s^{(d-1)/2} = |y|^{(d-1)/2} that eq:T_NIG silently drops when it asserts that the boundary growth is controlled by h_1^{NIG}. Consequence: at the critical choice Sigma tilde = 2/(delta^2 T^2) Delta^{-1} the exponent -delta T t + s vanishes identically and r^{NIG}(u) ~ const * |Psi^{-1}(u)|^{(d-1)/2} -> +infinity for every d>1, i.e. case (ii) of eq:mnig_conditions-2 is misclassified (it is +infinity, not sqrt(det(Sigma tilde))). Only cases (i) and (iii) survive, since there the exponential dominates the polynomial.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the asymptotic quotient keeping the factors (q/2)^{v/2} and 1/sqrt(2s), reclassify case (ii) as divergence for d>1, and impose the strict inequality delta^2 T^2 Delta - 2 Sigma tilde^{-1} > 0 (e.g. Sigma tilde = (1+eps) 2/(delta^2 T^2) Delta^{-1}), re-solving the minimum-determinant trade-off; or explicitly invoke the payoff transform's decay to absorb the polynomial growth.
issues.overall_effect: The stated sufficient condition 'delta^2 T^2 Delta - 2 Sigma tilde^{-1} >= 0' is not sufficient at equality, and the matrix actually constructed and used (Sigma tilde = 2/(delta^2 T^2) Delta^{-1}, summarized in Table tab:multivariate_dom_tranf and used for all dependent-asset NIG experiments with d = 3,4,6,10,15) leaves the ratio r^{NIG} unbounded at the boundary, so the paper's own singularity-avoidance argument and the derived boundary-growth rule for multivariate NIG fail for d>1.
issues.title: Multivariate NIG boundary term h_1^{NIG} drops the polynomial factor of the Bessel asymptotics
issues.why_classification: The missing factor is identified by the paper's own two preceding asymptotic displays, so the repair is a contained re-derivation and a re-optimization of one matrix choice; the framework, the other two models and all experiments remain recognizably intact. It is not a local sign fix (the minimum-determinant solution is no longer admissible), so it exceeds minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} g(\boldsymbol{y}) d\boldsymbol{y} =  \int_{0}^{+\infty} \left(   \int_{[0,1]^d} \frac{g\left( w \boldsymbol{\tilde{L}} \cdot \Psi_{nor}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{u}; \boldsymbol{I_d}) \right)}{\psi_{lap}\left( w\boldsymbol{\tilde{L}} \cdot \Psi_{nor}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{u}; \boldsymbol{I_d})  \right)} d\boldsymbol{u} \right)     \psi_{ray}(w) dw,
where $\psi_{ray}(w) = 2 w \exp(-w^2)$ denotes the PDF of the Rayleigh distribution with scale $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
where $\{y_m\}_{m = 1}^{M_{Lag}}$ and $\{\omega_m\}_{m = 1}^{M_{Lag}}$ are the Gauss--Laguerre quadrature nodes and quadrature weights, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: In the estimator the outer variable w of Proposition prop:nig_proposition is never bound: the m-th Gauss-Laguerre node y_m is summed over, but the integrand is evaluated at the free symbol w, so the summand cannot be computed. In addition the mixing density is written as psi_{sqrt{W}}(y_m), a symbol that is nowhere defined (Proposition prop:nig_proposition and its proof denote the same Rayleigh density by psi_ray). Two distinct corrections are needed (w -> y_m and psi_{sqrt{W}} -> psi_ray) before the estimator is an evaluable object, so this is not a single forced typo.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace w by the quadrature node y_m inside the summand and use the already defined Rayleigh density psi_ray(y_m) as the outer weight, consistent with the quadrature rule sum_m (omega_m/lambda_Lag(y_m)) F(y_m) psi_ray(y_m).
issues.overall_effect: The hybrid Gauss-Laguerre/RQMC scheme that prices NIG options under dependent assets is not executable as printed; the NIG multivariate pricing algorithm has no well-defined input-output map until the formula is repaired.
issues.title: NIG hybrid Gauss-Laguerre/RQMC estimator is ill defined (unbound w and undefined density)
issues.why_classification: Both fixes are local symbol substitutions dictated by Proposition prop:nig_proposition and by the stated Gauss-Laguerre rule; the method, its guarantee and all experiments are preserved once the symbols are bound.
